title: A concrete quotient-cone model for the canonical scalar-extension pullback comparison
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, finite extensions $E\subset L$ of $\mathbf Q_\ell$, valuation rings $\mathcal O_E\subset\mathcal O_L$, and uniformizers $\varpi_E,\varpi_L$ [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $g:X\to Y$ be a scheme isomorphism with $\ell$ invertible [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. On the small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $R_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,W}$, $S_W=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{L,W}$, $A_{F,m}=\mathcal O_F/\varpi_F^m$ and $B_{F,W,m}=(A_{F,m})_W$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients]. The canonical $R_W$-module $S_W$ is finite free. Write $C_WH=H\otimes^L_{R_W}S_W$ and $T_WH$ for integral scalar extension [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], with its specified natural completion comparison $\chi_{W,H}:C_WH\to T_WH$ on derived-complete $H$ [lem-weil-finite-free-completed-scalar-comparison].

Let $K\in D^b_c(Y,\mathcal O_E)$ [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], choose a flat-term K-flat resolution $P\to K$ [def-pc-kflat-complex, lem-pc-kflat-resolution], and put $Q=P\otimes_{R_Y}S_Y$. Then $Q$ is flat-term K-flat over $S_Y$ and represents $C_YK$. Define
$$P_{E,m}=P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{E,Y,m},\qquad Q_{L,m}=Q\otimes_{S_Y}B_{L,Y,m}=P\otimes_{R_Y}B_{L,Y,m}.$$
Here $R_Y\to B_{L,Y,m}$ is precisely the same-index map $\rho_m=(\iota_m)_Y\pi^E_m$ of [def-weil-integral-scalar-extension], with $\iota_m:A_{E,m}\to A_{L,m}$.
For $F=E,L$ and a flat-term K-flat complex $M$ over $\widehat{\mathcal O}_{F,Y}$, put
$$D^F_m(M)=\operatorname{Res}^F_m g_{F,m}^*(M\otimes B_{F,Y,m}),\qquad A_F(M)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_mD^F_m(M)\to\prod_mD^F_m(M))[-1],$$
where $g_{F,m}^*$ is finite module pullback and $s$ is induced by quotient transitions [def-pur-integral-derived-operations]. Thus $A_E(P)$ represents $Lg_E^*K$, and $A_L(Q)$ represents $Lg_L^*(C_YK)$.

There is a specified map of strict towers of $S_X$-complexes
$$d_m:D^E_m(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X\longrightarrow D^L_m(Q).$$
It is the change-of-rings map induced by $P_{E,m}\to Q_{L,m}$, $p\otimes\bar a\mapsto p\otimes\iota_m(\bar a)$, by the coefficient structure maps of $g^{-1}$ [def-weil-proetale-inverse-image], and by $S_X\to B_{L,X,m}$. Equivalently, on local tensor generators its formula is
$$((g^{-1}(p\otimes\bar a))\otimes b)\otimes s\longmapsto (g^{-1}(p\otimes\iota_m(\bar a)))\otimes\bigl(\iota_m(b)\pi^L_m(s)\bigr),$$
where $\bar a$ is a local section of $B_{E,Y,m}$ inside inverse image, $b$ of $B_{E,X,m}$, and $s$ of $S_X$. Tensor products mean sheaf tensor products [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].
Since $S_X$ is finite free, the canonical tensor/product maps identify $A_E(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X$ with the Roos cone of $D^E_\bullet(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X$. Let
$$\delta_P:A_E(P)\otimes_{R_X}S_X\longrightarrow A_L(Q)$$
be the resulting cone map induced by $d_\bullet$; on cone coordinates it is $(b,a)\mapsto((\prod_m d_m)b,(\prod_m d_m)a)$ after these canonical tensor/product identifications. In particular both coordinates are specified.

Let $B(P)=\operatorname{Cone}(1-s:\prod_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mQ_{L,m}\to\prod_m\operatorname{Res}^L_mQ_{L,m})[-1]$, representing $T_YK$. The chain map
$$\chi_Y(P):Q\to B(P),\quad q\mapsto(0,(q\bmod\varpi_L^m)_m)$$
represents $\chi_{Y,K}$ and is a quasi-isomorphism. The map $\delta_P$ is a quasi-isomorphism and the canonical tensor-and-completion scalar-extension comparison is the following specified derived morphism:
$$\alpha_K=Lg_L^*(\chi_{Y,K})\circ[\delta_P]\circ\chi_{X,Lg_E^*K}^{-1}:T_X(Lg_E^*K)\longrightarrow Lg_L^*(T_YK).$$
All identifications here are the canonical resolution comparisons of [lem-pur-integral-operations-well-defined]; the formula is independent of $P$ and natural in $K$. It specifies the canonical comparison described by ordinary tensor associativity and strict quotient-tower completion in [lem-pur-integral-operations-scalar-extension], rather than an arbitrary isomorphism between its two objects. The brackets denote localization at quasi-isomorphisms [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: Apply integralOperations_preserve_constructible to K and take the completeness component of the resulting sfIntegralConstructible proof. For every good representative P, scalarGood shows that its ordinary scalar extension is again good.

The normalization equation of scalarCompletion_existsUnique identifies the localized completion chain map on P. Naturality along e inverse gives the displayed representative equation at K. Its left side is a composite of isomorphisms, since K is complete. Cancel the two ordinary representative isomorphisms on the right to prove that the localized completion chain map is an isomorphism. DerivedCategory.isIso_Q_map_iff_quasiIso then proves that the chain map is a quasi-isomorphism.

The defining normalization equation of scalarPullbackOrdinary_existsUnique equates the localized scalarPullbackChain, preceded by two representative isomorphisms, to a composite of isomorphisms. Cancel the two preceding isomorphisms and reflect invertibility through DerivedCategory.Q to obtain the quasi-isomorphism of this specific scalarPullbackChain. This uses the existing normalized comparison theorem, rather than reconstructing the ramified tower argument already underlying that theorem.

Expand scalarPullbackCompleted as conjugation of scalarPullbackOrdinary by the two completion isomorphisms. Substitute the representative normalization of scalarPullbackOrdinary, cancel the adjacent inverse comparison maps, and use its naturality along e inverse. Functoriality and the inverse identities for e give exactly the required representative formula.

Precompose the asserted naturality square by the source completion isomorphism and postcompose by the pullback of the inverse target completion isomorphism. Naturality of scalarCompletion moves each completion map past the given morphism. Cancel inverse pairs. The remaining square is scalarPullbackOrdinary naturality, so cancellation proves the original square for every derived morphism.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 3.5.1 and Lemmas 6.5.9(4), 6.8.2(1); H1 assembly from the existing normalized scalar comparison declarations. The shorter proof reflects their invertibility through DerivedCategory.Q and uses naturality and cancellation.
